title: Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken Movie: Guren no Kizuna-hen
content:
I always knew Slime fans feast like kings. I mean, with a premise as bare bone as this you’d think acing seasons and specials would be in the bag, but you’d be surprised with how much stale soup we get under the Isekai umbrella. Looking at you Arifureta.

Slime has always been the type of show where you’d turn off your mind and sit down and relax while watching. It totally works, no cognitive effort needed. This movie follows suit with that, but with a caveat.

You know the overtired analogy of kicking around a puppy? This movie was the personification of that. I guess I would not be able to stay off spoilers in this review because but my biggest gripe revolves around it.

So the movie kicks in with revealing that Benimaru and folks left a non blood brother friend behind when they escaped, only to reunite again during this movie. In classic film making, this is like establishing a new emotional link, a plot hostage of sort, that the events can escalate around and threaten to tragically resolve around. Sure, by the book and nothing new to boast about, but then again, this new “hostage” character, Hiiro, also has a strong emotional link with this other new character, Towa, which is conveniently very weak and sick, and danger is sneaking around her at every corner.

Fine, so far, all established threats are to be expected. But then the plot throws the first jab at Towa, making you feel like it’s the end for her, and while you’re preparing for your whole sad and snotty reaction, the plot decides to alternate the target of the tragedy and switch to Hiiro. So far you’re like “Haha, you got me”, and now you’re supposed to feel bad because of the attachment to Benimaru, but then the plot comes in clutch again and pulls the rug one more time, yet again switching back to Towa, and again, back to Hiiro. By the end of it, you’re no longer taking the stakes seriously, you’ve completely decided to not care, and have been completely desensitized towards any threats against either one of those two.

Oh no, it does not end there. Hiiro kills himself in sacrifice to save Towa. Shocking! Then plot gives you a few minutes to breath, just to suddenly bring Hiiro back to life, hug his queen and hope for a better future. But wait, is that an imminent threat I hear sneaking by? Too late, now Towa is being Thanosed. Hiiro and folks grieve for seconds after seeing her disappear in pain and agony. And BOOM, there she is again, magically materializing back, alive and healthier than ever in front of everyone.

That was a roller coaster if I have ever seen one. But for all the wrong reasons. Zero stakes.
That aside, I thought everything else was decent. Great action sequences, good character interactions. There was more of Diablo, so that’s a plus. And of course, fillery motives.

Overall: 7.2/10.
